charter:
# Charter — S04 action registry (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** S04 'Action registry — derive, manifest, OpenAPI, MCP, invocation, external ingest',
  track v1, ADM phase G, tranche 3, project `01a1d039-0d28-7eb6-a62a-f420e742595c`, plan
  `docs/plans/slices/S04-action-registry.md`. The record carries `meta.measured_status: built`,
  `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`, closed issue #3, the approved scope baseline
  `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` (approver `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`, taken 2026-11-22) and the approved charter gate
  `01a20255-6578-7a4d-b99b-81d6d03d8880`. The rework runs under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** deliver SPEC §8 S4 — 20 actions identical over HTTP and MCP — from one declaration
  per invocable operation, so the manifest, the OpenAPI operation, the MCP tool and the route
  cannot diverge. The tranche-3 review `01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9` closed the tranche on 2026-11-26 with
  S04 still carrying its record set; this retrospective completes the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle record
  for the slice (charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D
  artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project-brief
  and evidence outputs, and the closure review) rather than adding scope.
- **Scope:** the declaration and registry, the invocation path with tenancy, idempotency,
  deadline and transaction, the manifest and MCP projections, the OpenAPI fold and lock, the
  external `openapi.json` ingest, and the boot assertion that fails closed. Out of scope are the
  domain actions of S05–S11, `kind: workflow` execution (S13), the channel-`mcp` delivery rows
  (S06) and the signed `mcp_server` channel (S06-α).
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26; it records the slice
  delivered under closed issue #3 — the runtime resolution work merged at `6d215982d` (#766),
  the served registry and lock green — and does not authorise new construction.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S04 action registry (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

body.assignment: Rework S04 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and re-publish the project-brief and evidence outputs. The architecture work is the action registry itself — one `ActionSpec` per invocable operation projected into the manifest, the OpenAPI document, the MCP tool list and the router, with a fail-closed consistency assertion and an invocation path that composes tenancy, idempotency, deadline and transaction around every call.
body.scope: In scope: the charter and its approved gate `01a20255-6578-7a4d-b99b-81d6d03d8880`; the seven A–D artefacts and the five register kinds; the scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` with its approver `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`; the WBS deliverables recorded for the slice and their four WSJF inputs 8, 8, 13, 5; the delivery contract this pack authors at phase f; the Phase-G review citing the standing delegation; the project-brief and evidence outputs; and the closure on the closure gate `01a216d1-3255-7127-8835-a15916dcacf6`. Out of scope: the domain actions of S05–S11, workflow execution (S13), channel delivery rows (S06) and the signed MCP channel (S06-α); this rework adds no feature and re-opens no V1 slice.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the #526 rework delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; the Architecture Board reviews the seven A–D artefacts, which the factory records as approved. The programme owner is the approver of the delivery contract and of the closure; the scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` is approved by `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`, and the closure gate `01a216d1-3255-7127-8835-a15916dcacf6` was decided by an approver distinct from its requester. The slice's construction was delivered under closed issue #3, with the runtime resolution model merged on main at `6d215982d` and the served registry locked at `docs/design/data/actions.json`.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is executable and was proved: twenty actions identical over HTTP and MCP (`crates/actions/tests/parity_http_mcp.rs` compares `http.body` with `mcp.structuredContent`); one `spec_hash` across manifest, resolved operation and MCP tool; duplicate names, MCP collisions and out-of-charset names fail closed at boot; a schema-invalid input returns RFC 9457 with padded `errors[]` and never a 500; two identical POSTs with one key yield one `action_invocation`; and the served lock catches drift while a breaking ingest is refused with the approved version still serving. The runtime work merged at `6d215982d` adds the imported-action proof: an approved external row is discovered, invoked over HTTP and MCP, survives a restart, and a revoked approval answers typed absent.
body.contract: This statement is authored retrospectively under the delegation and is approved through the same board gate it describes; its approval is recorded by the factory from this pack, not asserted here. It is complemented by the delivery contract whose commitments, compliance, approval and capacity fields this pack authors on the approved scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` (kind scope, taken 2026-11-22, approved by `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`), and by the Phase-G review the factory records against that contract. The closure gate `01a216d1-3255-7127-8835-a15916dcacf6` and the `projects.close` approval recorded on 2026-11-26 are the gate the close reads.

artifacts.title: S04 Requirements Catalogue
artifacts.purpose: State the functional and non-functional requirements S04 must satisfy, with the proof each demands.
artifacts.scope: Derived from the S04 plan's declaration, invocation/MCP and OpenAPI/ingest sections; 16 internal and four external actions are in scope.

value.detail: ETag/If-None-Match wraps it and returns 304 on a match.
value.objective: GET /api/actions returns ActionManifest {actions:[{name,version,kind,spec_hash,scopes,idempotent,timeout_ms}], generated_at}.

value.detail: A spec_exempt fallback at /api/actions/{name}/invocations returns action-not-found.
value.objective: POST /api/actions/<literal name>/invocations accepts {input} and returns {output}.

value.detail: Each declares input/output schema, scope, idempotency and timeout.
value.objective: Provide 16 internal actions: actions.list, actions.describe, me.get, tenants.get, tenants.update_settings, members.list, members.set_role, departments.list, departments.create, audit.list, jobs.list, jobs.retry, schedules.list, schedules.upsert, events.list, licences.get.

value.detail: They are served by the external_actions.rs stub at CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_FIXTURES_URL.
value.objective: Ingest four external actions from crates/actions/tests/fixtures/external/openapi.json: fixtures.echo, fixtures.slow, fixtures.fail, fixtures.timeout.

value.detail: With request_id and duration_ms stripped, http.body equals mcp.structuredContent.
value.objective: All 20 actions behave identically over HTTP and MCP.

value.detail: Two identical POSTs with one key return the same status and body and leave one action_invocation; the loser replays the winner.
value.objective: Idempotency-Key is scoped (tenant_id, action name, key) and claimed by INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

value.detail: A timeout rolls the invocation transaction back; a separate short transaction records action_invocation(outcome='timeout') and audit_event(status='error').
value.objective: SET LOCAL statement_timeout = timeout_ms plus tokio::time::timeout bound every invocation.

value.detail: 4xx becomes action-external-refused, never a 500; 5xx becomes 502 action-upstream-failed; five failures in 30 s open the breaker (503 action-circuit-open, no upstream call).
value.objective: Map external outcomes to stable RFC 9457 problems.

# S04 Technology Standards Catalogue

## Metadata

Retrospective catalog for S04, authored 2026-11-26 from the record's own artefact row and the slice plan `docs/plans/slices/S04-action-registry.md`. Phase d, plateau hld, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; reviewer the Architecture Board; subject project `01a1d039-0d28-7eb6-a62a-f420e742595c`. The row this pack re-versions was authored on 2026-11-22 and carries `meta.record: #526`, so the content is the slice's own, not a restatement.

## Entries

The standards are those the plan pins. The Rust workspace and the `schemars`/JSON Schema pair keep one declaration and one schema; `rmcp` streamable HTTP is the MCP transport; `openapiv3` with `OpenApiRouter` folds and ingests OpenAPI; RFC 9457 problem details are the only error shape; PostgreSQL with row-level security holds the registry and the invocation state; and the workspace quality gate is the slice's own preflight. The rows below carry 8 entries; their `axis_a` and `axis_b` are the artefact's own vocabulary and the `value` object is the substance the §8.1 create action stores.

## Links

This artefact links to **S04 Stakeholder Map** as a `reuse`. The edge is the lifecycle order the standard seeds: the stakeholder questions shape the drivers, the drivers produce the requirements, the requirements select the solution, and the solution decomposes into capabilities, data and standards. No artefact in the set is an orphan.

## Document

The artefact's published document is `S04 Technology Standards Catalogue` — its category-`architecture-artifact-instance` body carries the same four sections and is the row the mandatory-artefact standard resolves its Document section from. The factory publishes the document before it binds the artefact, so the row pins a real body from its first version and the standard's instance rule finds it.

# Architecture Artefact Index — S04 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Metadata

The artefact set for S04 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the
Stakeholder map, the Driver/goal/objective catalogue, the Requirements catalogue and the Solution
concept at phase a, plateau psa; the Business capability map at phase b, plateau hld; and the Data
entity catalogue and Technology standards catalogue at phases c and d. Each carries an authored
body authored on 2026-11-26 and an entry set from the slice's own artefact rows; the owner is the
programme architect under the #526 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and
the subject is project `01a1d039-0d28-7eb6-a62a-f420e742595c`.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: Stakeholder map (matrix), Driver/goal/
objective (catalog), Requirements (catalog), Solution concept (diagram), Business capability map
(diagram), Data entity catalogue (catalog), Technology standards (catalog). Each row carries the
entries listed in its own artefact, from eight stakeholder rows through eight requirements and
eight technology standards; the factory re-versions the artefact rows this index names and binds
them to their instance documents.

## Links

The artefacts link in lifecycle order: stakeholder map → driver/goal/objective as a derivation,
driver → requirements as a derivation, requirements → solution concept as a derivation, solution →
capability map as a dependency, capability → data entity as a dependency, data → technology
standards as a dependency, and technology standards → stakeholder map as a reuse edge. Every
artefact in the set carries at least one link, so the standard's orphan rule finds no orphan.

## Document

This index is itself published as the category-`architecture-artifact` document for S04 and is
composed from the rows above. The per-artefact bodies are published as
category-`architecture-artifact-instance` documents, one per artefact, and it is those instance
documents the mandatory-artefact standard resolves its Document section from. The index is
regenerated by the factory from the same pack, so the two cannot diverge.

risk.title: A projection reads a second source and the four surfaces drift apart
risk.body: The failure mode the slice exists to prevent: once manifest, OpenAPI, MCP and router read anything other than the one `ActionSpec`, a change to one surface silently diverges from the others. The controls are `assert_registry_consistent` at boot, the single `spec_hash` per action and the served lock check; the retrospective review keeps them named so a later projection cannot be added outside the registry.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: An approved imported action is executable by a tenant that should not see it
risk.body: Resolution reads the tenant's approved `action_registry` row, so the approval gate — not a compiled-in allowlist — is the access control. The risk is a row approved for one tenant being resolved for another, or a revoked approval still serving. The controls are the scoped read in `resolve_action`, the typed `action-unavailable` refusal after revocation and the restart proof in `action_resolution.rs`.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

requirements: crates/actions/tests/action_resolution.rs — the revocation and restart proof

issue.title: The parity contract does not yet name S04's actions
issue.body: `parity/parity.yaml` and `parity/native.tsv` from S00 still carry `parity_ids: PENDING-S0` for this slice: the S00 trace obligation has not been closed for S04. It is not a gap in the S04 gate (HTTP/MCP identity), which the parity test proves, but it is an open record item and is carried as one rather than repaired by editing S00's contract from here.

issue.title: The pre-rework receipt was red on the delivery contract and the artefact set
issue.body: Before this pack, `docs/evidence/rework/S04.json` was red: the mandatory delivery-contract artefact was absent (P1) and seven standard artefacts were partial (P2). The pack supplies the contract and re-versions the artefacts; the receipt after the factory run is the statement of what changed, and the issue stays recorded so the red state is not hidden.

assumption.title: The record's own artefact rows are the slice's content of record
assumption.body: The seven artefacts authored on 2026-11-22 are treated as the slice's own architecture content; this rework re-versions them with their own entries and adds the authored bodies and links the standard requires, rather than re-deriving the architecture from the plan. The assumption holds because the rows carry `meta.record: #526` and their entries cite the plan's own traps, components and standards.

assumption.title: The library gate remains the slice's only construction proof
assumption.body: S04's gate is proved by the workspace test suite and the lock check, not by a live deployment of its own. The slice is consumed by S05–S11 through the same registry, so a regression that only a live consumer could see is not covered here; that coverage belongs to the consumer slices' acceptance.

dependency.title: S02 supplies the tenancy, audit and idempotency spine S04 invokes through
dependency.body: The invocation path composes the S02 `begin_scoped` transaction, the `audit_event` writer and the `idempotency_key` claim. A change to any of them changes S04's contract; the dependency is recorded as `needs` on the project record and is why S04 sits in tranche 3 after S02 and S03.

dependency.title: Every later slice adds actions through this registry, never a surface
dependency.body: S05–S11 declare their domain actions against `crates/actions`; the registry is therefore a downstream dependency of the whole product spine. The control is that a second source is forbidden — a slice that needs a new operation adds a declaration, and the projections follow from it.

benefit.title: One declaration means a surface cannot silently diverge
benefit.body: Every consumer reads the same `ActionSpec`: the manifest, the OpenAPI document, the MCP tool list and the router are projections of one value with one `spec_hash`. The benefit is structural — a change that would have needed four edits now needs one, and the lock check turns an accidental drift into a red build before release.

benefit.title: Retries are safe and auditable at the invocation boundary
benefit.body: The scoped idempotency claim means two identical POSTs with one key produce one `action_invocation` and the same response, and the deadline plus transaction bound every call so a retry replays a committed outcome rather than half of one. Operators can answer what ran, for whom, and with what result from the record alone.

body.commitments: Deliver SPEC §8 S4 as one governed slice: one `ActionSpec` per invocable operation projected into the manifest, the OpenAPI document, the MCP tool list and the router; a fail-closed registry consistency assertion at boot; an invocation path composing tenancy, idempotency, deadline and transaction; the external OpenAPI ingest whose breaking changes are held for approval; and the served lock that catches drift. The slice adds no surface and no second registry.
body.compliance: The Phase-G review the factory records from this pack carries the level compliant against this contract: it cites the standing delegation, the approved scope baseline, the closure gate decided by a distinct approver, the closed issue #3 and the evidence the gate actually produced — the parity test, the lock check, the ingest diff and the runtime resolution proof merged at `6d215982d`. A failing gate is recorded as non-conformant, never softened.
body.approval: The scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` is the approved baseline this contract rests on; its approver is `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545` and the charter gate `01a20255-6578-7a4d-b99b-81d6d03d8880` is approved. The contract itself is requested and approved through the board gate the factory drives, and the closure gate `01a216d1-3255-7127-8835-a15916dcacf6` and the `projects.close` approval recorded on 2026-11-26 are the gate the close reads.
body.capacity: The unit is the slice's accepted WBS deliverables — the ActionSpec derive crate and the registry and spec vocabularies — with the sixteen internal actions and the invocation, manifest, MCP, OpenAPI and boot work packages. The WBS carries WSJF 8, 8, 13, 5, and no work package outside the slice's scope is carried by this contract.
body.acceptance: Acceptance is executable: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions` over the parity, invocation, idempotency, ingest-diff, timeout and runtime-resolution targets; the served lock check exits 0; a duplicate registration exits 1 before bind; and a schema-invalid request returns RFC 9457 with populated `errors[]`. The manifest `acceptance/programme/S04.toml` executes the same properties against the record.
body.evidence: The evidence route is the committed proof: `crates/actions/tests/parity_http_mcp.rs` for the HTTP/MCP identity, `served-spec.lock.json` for the contract, `crates/actions/tests/action_resolution.rs` for the imported-action round trip, and `docs/design/data/actions.json` for the served registry. The registry this slice declares is live at 593 actions, 569 internal and 24 external, with the four `fixtures.*` external actions the gate names.

wbs_deliverable.title: The action registry and its execution contract

review.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review, dated 2026-11-26, records the level compliant against the delivery contract created from this pack. The slice is recorded as built under closed issue #3: the scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` is approved by `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`, the charter gate `01a20255-6578-7a4d-b99b-81d6d03d8880` is approved, the closure gate `01a216d1-3255-7127-8835-a15916dcacf6` was decided by an approver distinct from its requester, the WBS deliverables carry WSJF 8, 8, 13, 5, both accepted deliverables carry demo credits, and no open P0 product finding remains. The construction itself was delivered twice over: the V1 slice proved the compiled registry and its four projections, and the runtime resolution model merged on main at `6d215982d` (#766) proved an imported approved action resolving through the same surfaces, over HTTP and MCP, across a restart and after revocation, with the path/query bindings and the tenant bearer. The pre-rework receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S04.json` was red: the mandatory delivery-contract artefact was absent and seven standard artefacts were partial. This pack supplies the authored record and the factory writes it as live rows, so the review records compliant on the completed record while keeping the pre-rework gap visible.

project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — S04 Action registry (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

One declaration per invocable operation, projected into the manifest, the OpenAPI document, the
MCP tool list and the router, so HTTP and MCP cannot diverge. The slice's gate is twenty actions
identical over HTTP and MCP, proved by the parity test over the sixteen internal and four
`fixtures.*` external actions, with one `spec_hash` across all four projections.

## Boundary

In: the `ActionSpec` declaration and `#[action]` derive, the compile-time registry and its boot
assertion, `GET /api/actions`, `POST /api/actions/{name}/invocations` with idempotency, deadline,
audit and transaction, `rmcp` at `/mcp`, the OpenAPI fold and lock, the `openapiv3` ingest, and
`migrations/0003_action_registry.sql`. Out: domain actions (S05–S11), workflow execution (S13),
channel-`mcp` delivery rows (S06) and the signed `mcp_server` channel (S06-α).

## Reuse sources

The fr registry's `Capability` field set and generation approach; the agent runtime catalog's
`OpDef`, `PinnedCatalog::from_rows`, `effective_level` and outputs. The slice carries the field
set and the closed `effect`/`confirm`/`tenancy` vocabularies, not Zod, not a legacy handler.

## Inception units

The sixteen internal actions and the four external fixtures, the invocation path, the manifest
and MCP projections, the OpenAPI fold and lock, the ingest diff and the boot assertion — the
work packages recorded in the project WBS.

## Dependencies

S02 supplies the tenancy, audit and idempotency spine; S03 the domain aggregates and transitions
the domain actions build on. Every later slice adds actions through this registry, never a
surface.

## Acceptance

`cargo test -p conveyor-actions` over the parity, invocation, idempotency, ingest, timeout and
runtime-resolution targets; the served lock check exits 0; a duplicate registration exits 1
before bind; schema-invalid input returns RFC 9457 with populated `errors[]`; and the imported
action round trip serves over HTTP and MCP across a restart.

## Capabilities

Action declaration and projection, a fail-closed registry, idempotent invocation, external action
ingest under the same contract, contained outbound failures, MCP parity and the OpenAPI lock.

## Plan

`docs/plans/slices/S04-action-registry.md`; programme project tier 1 of tranche 3; the runtime
resolution follow-up merged at `6d215982d`.

# Evidence — S04 Action registry (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Claim

The slice's gate holds: twenty actions behave identically over HTTP and MCP; the manifest,
resolved operation and MCP tool share one `spec_hash`; a duplicate or out-of-charset name fails
closed before bind; a schema-invalid input returns RFC 9457 with populated `errors[]`; an
idempotent replay yields one `action_invocation`; and the served lock catches drift while a
breaking ingest is refused. An approved imported action resolves through the same surfaces,
survives a restart, and a revoked approval answers typed unavailable.

## Evidence

`crates/actions/tests/parity_http_mcp.rs` compares `http.body` with `mcp.structuredContent` for
all twenty actions. `crates/actions/tests/action_resolution.rs` proves the imported round trip
over HTTP and MCP with path/query bindings and the tenant bearer, across a restart and after
revocation. `docs/design/data/actions.json` is the served registry at 593 actions (569 internal,
24 external) and `served-spec.lock.json` is the locked contract. The project record carries the
approved scope baseline, the approved charter gate and the closure gate decided by a distinct
approver.

## Verification

The commands are the slice's own: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions`, the server's
`--print-openapi --check-lock`, a duplicate-registration serve that exits 1, and the manifest
`acceptance/programme/S04.toml` executed by `scripts/verify-project.py`. The rework receipt
`docs/evidence/rework/S04.json` is the statement of the record before and after this pack.

## Links

Plan `docs/plans/slices/S04-action-registry.md`; project `01a1d039-0d28-7eb6-a62a-f420e742595c`;
issue #3 closed, runtime merge `6d215982d`; tranche-3 review
`01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9`.

## Gap

The parity contract from S00 does not yet name this slice's actions (`parity_ids:
PENDING-S0`). It is an S00 trace obligation, not a gap in the S04 gate, and it is carried as an
open register item rather than edited from here.

closure_review:
# Closure review — S04 action registry (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is SPEC §8 S4: twenty actions identical over HTTP and MCP from
one declaration. The record supports it — the slice is recorded as built under closed issue #3,
the scope baseline is approved by `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`, the closure gate was
decided by an approver distinct from its requester, the charter gate is approved, the WBS
deliverables carry WSJF 8, 8, 13, 5, both accepted deliverables carry demo credits, and the
declared outputs project-brief and evidence are published. The runtime resolution model merged
at `6d215982d` extends the same contract to imported external actions. Against that, the
pre-rework receipt was red on the delivery contract and seven partial artefacts; this pack
supplies the rows those checks read, so the acceptance is met on the completed record rather than
on the earlier red one.

## Evidence

The evidence is the snapshot record: project `01a1d039-0d28-7eb6-a62a-f420e742595c`, the approved
scope baseline `01a20256-44d0-731d-b345-fffc5f3ac9e8` with its approver, closed issue #3, the
tranche-3 review `01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9`, and the published outputs of
2026-11-26 — project brief, evidence, architecture artefact index, project registers, project WBS
and closure review. The seven A–D artefacts, the five register kinds, the delivery contract and
the WBS deliverable are the records this pack authors and the factory writes; the parity,
resolution and lock tests are the construction proof they cite.

## Open items

Two items remain visible. First, the slice's parity contract from S00 still carries
`parity_ids: PENDING-S0`; the S04 gate does not depend on it, but it is an open S00 trace
obligation and is recorded as such rather than repaired from here. Second, the record is
reconstructed from the snapshot facts and the existing receipt; it evidences the lifecycle and
its gate decisions rather than replaying every construction step. Neither item is a scope gap and
neither is waived.

## Decision

The retrospective decision is to close S04 on the record the rework completes, at the level
compliant that the Phase-G review records against the delivery contract this pack authors, with
the pre-rework red receipt and the S00 trace obligation named rather than hidden. The decision is
dated 2026-11-26 and rests on the approved baseline, the distinct closure approver, closed issue
#3 and the published outputs; it does not add scope, does not reclassify any earlier row, and
does not assert a re-measurement of the slice's original construction.
